skill.name: codex-pet
skill.description: Creates Codex-compatible custom pets from a reference image using RunComfy GPT Image 2 and ImageMagick. It guides canonical pose generation, sprite atlas assembly, manifest creation, and local installation.
skill.summary: Generate a Codex Pet sprite atlas and manifest from one reference image.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown false positives, but the workflow still performs real external CLI, network, credential, and hidden filesystem operations. Confirmed risks include global package installation, RunComfy token use, image processing through third-party services, and writes into Codex configuration paths. I found no prompt injection attempt in the skill text.

remediation.issue: Pet names are used directly in filesystem paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate pet names with a strict slug rule and reject slashes, dots, empty names, and path traversal text before creating paths.

remediation.issue: The workflow depends on RUNCOMFY_TOKEN and local token storage.
remediation.suggestion: Document token scope, revocation, and log hygiene. Prefer environment variables for CI and avoid printing token-bearing commands.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs global package installation and external CLI execution.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, pin trusted package versions where possible, and show commands before execution.

remediation.issue: Source image URLs are sent to a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to provide confidential images and request consent before sending any URL to RunComfy.

remediation.issue: Generated files are written into hidden Codex configuration paths.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the destination path, confirm it remains under CODEX_HOME/pets, and ask before overwriting existing pet files.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Pet Name Used in Filesystem Paths
semantic_findings.description: PET_NAME is interpolated into RUN_DIR and DEST without validation. A name containing path traversal text could write generated files outside the intended pet folder.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shell snippets use PET_NAME directly in directory paths and copy commands. The example value is safe, but the skill gives no validation rule for user-supplied names.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Image Processing Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends a user-provided source image URL to RunComfy for remote GPT Image 2 processing. Confidential images or image-based prompt injection can cross this boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The runcomfy command passes SOURCE_URL as image input, and the security section states external URLs are fetched by RunComfy. This is intentional but security-relevant.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a Codex Pet sprite sheet and a pet manifest for local Codex installation.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: It requires the RunComfy CLI, ImageMagick, and a valid RUNCOMFY_TOKEN.

faq.question: Does it need Codex Pro?
faq.answer: No. The workflow uses RunComfy GPT Image 2 instead of the Codex imagegen skill.

faq.question: Where are files installed?
faq.answer: The final files are copied into the local Codex pets folder under CODEX_HOME.

faq.question: Can I customize animation?
faq.answer: Yes. The ImageMagick transform values can be adjusted while keeping the fixed atlas contract.

faq.question: What privacy boundary should I know?
faq.answer: The source image URL is sent to RunComfy for remote image generation.
